sealedSource: Structurally modelled on deepwater well-integrity decisions where ambiguous pressure tests were resolved toward the commercially convenient reading.
archetype: Ambiguous signal reinterpreted toward the commercially convenient reading; displaced cost to environment and third parties.
historicallySupportedMechanisms: Contradictory integrity-test results were not resolved before the irreversible next step.
Schedule and cost pressure selected the convenient interpretation of ambiguous evidence.
Absence of formal objection was treated as agreement despite stated disagreement.
materialisedConsequences: Loss of life among the crew
Long-duration release into the marine environment
Economic harm to coastal fishing and tourism communities who had no part in the decision
Costs exceeding the saved time by many orders of magnitude
irreversibleThreshold: Marine ecosystem damage and human death — neither reversible.
absentStakeholder: Coastal communities and the marine environment; also the crew, who were present but not consulted.
narratorContribution: The narrator treated the absence of formal objection as agreement, and selected between two contradictory readings on cost grounds rather than resolving the contradiction.
horizonMismatch: Decision horizon hours; ecological recovery horizon decades; narrator recorded it as unknown.

availableActionsAtDecisionPoint.action: Run the further diagnostic test before displacement rather than choose between contradictory readings on schedule grounds.
Pause displacement until the contradictory pressure-test interpretations are reconciled.

plausibleUnrealisedRisks: Delay could create additional rig/schedule cost and contractual pressure.
irrelevantDistractors: A regulatory fine for schedule overrun as the principal risk
nonTargetHistoricalEvents: Crew fatigue may have been present but did not drive the keyed outcome.
